rv.q: Jackson's jazz-soaked, somewhat 'Enron'-tinged production is a hoot from start to finish.
After a much-praised run at Stratford, the RSC's best piece of new writing in years settles triumphantly into its London berth.
Heffernan's performance is superb: affable and charismatic yet slightly aloof, as the play wears on he retreats further into his core, his stare increasingly distant.
Some odd touches...did little to detract from a deeply thought-provoking, compelling and important new work.
On the whole, Morton-Smith's operatic vision is executed faultlessly: ingeniously conceived and well performed, fizzily written yet heavy-weight – Oppenheimer is a nuclear success.

cn.t: Morton-Smith's ambitious three-hour epic about the father of the atomic bomb earns strong praise for its stylish direction, impeccable performances, and unashamed scope in tackling nuclear physics for the stage.
